doc.title: Jim Cullum interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007

title: Beiderbecke Festival, Davenport visits and Bix films
summary: Cullum has not attended the festival due to Stanford commitments but visited Davenport and the Beiderbecke House; he mentions films on Bix.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: Have you ever been to the annual Beiderbecke Festival in Davenport?

Uh you know I’ve never been to that because they always hold it at late July and we’re always involved , we’ve been involved at Stanford for years and years and years. And so I’ve never been available. I’ve been asked. I have been to Davenport three times, been to the Beiderbecke House, I’ve played the Beiderbecke cornet and I went there for his hundredth anniversary of his birth. We had people from around the world there and we went to the Beiderbecke House and were there right at the moment that he was born in that house, and you know, and did all that stuff. We’re cultists. There’s a cult.
There was a film that Bob Wilber was involved with, right?

Yes. Yes, that’s right. There’s a film. But the best thing I think is there was a documentary done by a Canadian lady, it’s the best thing. It interviewed Hoagy Carmichael and others. It’s the best thing that’s been done as a film. And I guess people that go to the internet find it now.
